item.title: Hunger in Healdsburg – A Community Conversation — Thu Oct 1, 10:30 AM — Abel De Luna Community Center
item.description:
**Hunger is happening in Healdsburg—and Healdsburg organizations are stepping up to help.**
Food insecurity affects thousands of individuals and families in Healdsburg—neighbors who are working, raising families, and contributing to our community, yet still struggling to put enough food on the table.
**Hunger in Healdsburg: A Community Conversation** brings together local hunger relief organizations, community leaders, and residents for an open and informative dialogue about food insecurity in Healdsburg. This event is free for all to attend and is designed to create space for listening, learning, and connection—centering the voices of organizations that are directly serving our community.
Hosted by the Redwood Empire Food Bank, in partnership with the City of Healdsburg, this event will highlight:

item.title: Color Lab with Lena Wolff — Sat Oct 3, 11:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Color Lab was designed for everyone interested in learning how to experiment with color in new ways. Structured to convey the basics of color theory through hands-on practice, the workshop walks through a sequence of fun, approachable exercises in paint-mixing and collage. In-between art activities, a slideshow is presented that shares information on the biology of color vision, a breakdown of the essential properties of color, and the wondrous phenomenon of color relativity, with visual examples from the early color theorists, textiles, folk-art, and work by contemporary artists.
By the end of the workshop, participants will leave with a small set of color charts and collages, and fodder for a lifetime of future experimentation.
Open to absolute beginners, practicing artists, designers, and craftspeople alike. Older teens with a serious interest in art are also welcome to register.
$195- Member/$200-Non-member \( includes materials\). 14 students max.
--

item.description:
The 24th Annual California Jug Band Festival Brings a Century-Old American Musical Tradition to Petaluma
Free all-ages music festival at Lagunitas Brewing Company features five California jug bands and an open community jam.
PETALUMA, CA — The California Jug Band Association is bringing the 24th Annual California Jug Band Festival to Petaluma for the first time on Saturday, October 3, with a full day of free music celebrating one of America’s most distinctive and often-overlooked musical traditions.
The 2026 lineup brings together jug band musicians from throughout California, including groups from the North Bay, East Bay, and Santa Cruz area. While the participating bands perform in a variety of musical styles throughout the year, each will be leaning into its jug band repertoire for the festival.

item.title: S.R. Laws - Original Acoustic Songwriter — Sat Oct 3, 6:00 PM — Ferry Taproom
item.description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique. He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove.
Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Oct 4, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park — Sun Oct 4, 10:00 AM — Jack London State Historic Park
item.description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.
Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures. An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.
The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

item.title: Fall Wreath-Making — Sun Oct 4, 12:00 PM — Art Escape Sonoma
item.description:
Embrace the beauty of autumn and join us for a Fall Wreath-Making workshop that will leave your front door adorned with seasonal splendor! In this class you will learn how to create a lush and fragrant holiday wreath using a wire frame and foliage, branches, and other dried materials. Whether you're a novice or a seasoned crafter, this workshop offers a warm and welcoming environment for all skill levels.
Silvia Bagnacani is a professional artist, educator, and floral designer with a passion for celebrating the beauty of seasonal blooms. Known around Sonoma for her inspiring floral arranging and wreath-making workshops, Silvia thoughtfully sources local flowers and foliage to create stunning, nature-inspired designs.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Step Into Wonder - The Letting Go Art Experience — Sun Oct 4, 12:00 PM — Mare Island Art Studios
item.description:
An all-ages community art experience where visitors are invited to paint, draw, explore, and add their marks to collaborative artworks that will continue to evolve throughout the month. Come once or return each Sunday to see how the galleries change as the community creates together.
Wonder Sundays are free, all-ages afternoons inside Step Into Wonder: The Letting Go Art Experience—an immersive, evolving world of glowing sculpture, music, creative play, and collaborative art.
You won’t simply look at the art. You’ll become part of it.
Explore the installations, respond to creative prompts, add your own marks to the gallery, move, play, reflect, and follow your curiosity. Each Sunday, visitors will contribute something new, allowing the space to grow and transform throughout the month.
No artistic experience is needed, and there is no right or wrong way to participate. Come as you are, stay for as long as you like, and give yourself permission to create freely.
Source: North Bay Bo
